FIELD REFERENCE

Pacific herring habitat: where Clupea pallasii lives

Pacific herring (Clupea pallasii) live in coastal waters on both sides of the North Pacific. Their eastern range extends from Baja California to Alaska’s Beaufort Sea. Look at habitat by life stage: young fish use sheltered bays and inlets, while spawning adults deposit eggs on shallow coastal vegetation.

Updated 2026-11-18 · Castward

Where are Pacific herring found?

Key factDetail
Eastern Pacific rangeBaja California to the Beaufort Sea, Alaska
Young fishSheltered bays and inlets
Spawning habitatIntertidal and shallow subtidal shorelines; kelp and eelgrass
Other habitatInshore and offshore ocean waters

What should you know about pacific herring?

Are Pacific herring coastal fish?

Yes. NOAA describes a coastal schooling species on both sides of the Pacific. DFO records both inshore and offshore habitat.

Where do young Pacific herring live?

Alaska Fish and Game describes sheltered bays and inlets before juveniles move to deeper water.

Where do Pacific herring lay their eggs?

NOAA identifies kelp, eelgrass and other structures along intertidal and shallow subtidal shorelines.

Do all Pacific herring spawn in the same month?

No. NOAA states that spawning timing varies with latitude. Check the local stock and area.

Does a herring habitat record show where I can fish?

No. Confirm local access, open dates and permitted gear with the fisheries authority before a trip.
